history.notes: Per-device state provenance, read from Bond's own schema markers. Bond's devices/schemas.yaml documents five device properties as "(Bridge-only)": addr, freq, bps, zero_gap, and trust_state ("whether or not the Bond should trust its toggleable state belief ... and is `false` by default"). A device publishing any of them is proven bridge-learned RF by Bond's OWN record rather than merely inferred from the GX type, and the new read-only State Provenance property says so: "Bridge-learned RF (Bond-tracked belief)". For that device the state label tightens from "On (assumed - Bond's tracked belief)" to "On (assumed - a one-way RF belief the bridge tracks; the hand-held remote bypasses it undetectably)". · trust_state: false is Bond itself declining to trust its own belief, so it is surfaced rather than swallowed: State Provenance appends "- Bond itself marks this belief untrusted (trust_state: false)", and Device Status carries the same line on every refresh. The documentation explains what Bond documents about the flag (Bridge-only, present only where a Toggle command exists, false by default) and says plainly that what flips it true is not documented and is not guessed at here. · The sharpening is ONE-DIRECTIONAL. A device publishing none of those markers changes in no way at all — and, importantly, that is not a weakening: the one-way contract for a GX device rests on the device TYPE, not on a marker, so a missing marker proves nothing in either direction. The default assumed label stays byte-for-byte what it was, pinned by a test so a future edit cannot drift it, and no provenance path anywhere can emit the words measured, native, or confirmed. · The /properties read is now structure-aware where it used to be a flat pattern sweep. Marker detection is a TOP-LEVEL key check with a quote-aware scan, so a device named "Vent [attic" is text rather than structure, and an addr buried in a sub-object can no longer sharpen a label on evidence Bond never gave. Only trust_state's value is interpreted; the four radio markers count by presence alone, so a garbage or non-finite freq can neither change the verdict nor reach a clamp, a timer, or a wire body. · Provenance dies with the binding. A change of Device ID or Bond IP clears it silently along with every other learned fact, so device B never inherits device A's verdict and A's trust_state: false never keeps shouting about a device this driver has never read. · No new variables and no new events. POWER_ASSUMED keeps its exact meaning (1 = a belief is held, 0 = nothing observed yet), event ids are untouched, and provenance moves no variable — it changes only how honestly the same belief is described.

Points a Bond light at the right driver. A device reporting type LT is now routed to IntegrateIT Bond Light, which shipped after this driver did; the refusal, the Device Type property, and the List Bond Devices listing previously all sent you to the older poll-only IntegrateIT Bond driver. · Closes a gap where a malformed device record could be commanded. Bond marks a device type as required - a record that arrives without one is now refused by name instead of being treated as not-read-yet and blind-commanded off its advertised action list. · A corrupted Poll Interval (s) can no longer stall state feedback (a nan-millisecond timer never fires again), and the single point where a Bond action is transmitted now refuses a non-finite argument outright - the same two-layer hardening the rest of the Bond family receives in today's patches. · The pre-read window is unchanged: before the device record has been read, the four power commands are still attempted once and the bridge's own answer is surfaced. Refusing on no evidence would be inventing a verdict. · Documentation updated for the new routing and the typeless-record refusal.

Initial release candidate: dedicated single-device control of a Bond generic device (device type GX) over the Bond Home local API v2 (github.com/bondhome/api-v2). · Advertised-only control surface: GET /v2/devices/<id> supplies the device's own actions array, and once it is known an action absent from it is refused LOCALLY by name with the reason — nothing reaches the wire. Power On/Off, Toggle Power, and Stop map to TurnOn/TurnOff/TogglePower/Stop; Run Advertised Action reaches any other advertised action by name with an optional numeric argument, and requires the list rather than guessing. · One device type: a device reporting CF / MS / FP / LT is refused by name and pointed at the IntegrateIT driver that models it (Bond Ceiling Fan, Bond Shade, Bond Fireplace, or the poll-only Bond driver for a light). List Bond Devices annotates every enumerated device with its owning driver. · Assumed-state contract: a GX device is a learned one-way RF target with no return path, so Bond's /state is Bond's TRACKED BELIEF, not a measurement, and the original hand-held remote bypasses Bond entirely and silently desyncs that belief. POWER is published alongside POWER_ASSUMED and a Power State property that spells "assumed" out loud, in the same one-way honesty register as the Bond Shade, Somfy URTSI II, and ESI R2D7 drivers. Unknown at boot and after any rebind. · Real push state feedback via the Bond Push UDP Protocol (BPUP) listener on UDP port 30007: keep-alive subscription, \n-delimited JSON frame parsing tolerant of arbitrary datagram boundaries and junk, topic-filtered to this device, and resubscribe before the 125s bridge drop. · Automatic fallback to hash-gated HTTP polling of /state when BPUP goes silent, with a bounded 429 Retry-After backoff; the Feedback Mode property reports which path is live and why it fell back. · Publishes POWER, POWER_ASSUMED, and DEVICE_ONLINE with transition-only events (unknown->known baseline adoption is silent); reachability reports the bridge answering, never the RF link. · BOND-Token header auth (user-supplied, never logged), LAN-only destination guard enforced at the single transport chokepoint so control, polling, AND the boot-time metadata reads are all covered, with an Allow WAN Bond override, and MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing re-checked at wire-write time on every control path. · Known limits: one generic device per instance; GX only; power state is assumed and a press on the original remote is undetectable; BPUP needs UDP 30007 reachable or the driver runs poll-only; acceptance on physical hardware is not yet attached to this release.
